title: ACCSystem open-reference and multi-path design readiness register
root_cause_definition: One root-reference unit is one unique, non-empty identifier in open_decisions on any active registry row; repeated row appearances are deduplicated. This is a reproducible count of distinct gate/source-reference roots, not a claim that every ID is a distinct real-world policy issue. Cross-linked aliases remain separately identified and are explicitly related where the source review supports it.

design_status_definitions.RUNTIME_SELECTABLE: The architecture model defines at least two source-supported paths behind one shared contract, a scoped selection context, source-derived acceptance criteria for every path, and failure/recovery/audit/security handling. This is design-level only; it does not prove runtime code exists or owner approval.
design_status_definitions.IMPLEMENTED_MULTI_PATH: Reserved for a runtime implementation with linked, executed path-acceptance evidence. Documentation alone cannot receive this status.
design_status_definitions.DESIGN_REVIEW_REQUIRED: The review-to-registry linkage or scope evidence conflicts or is incomplete; do not count as runtime-selectable until reconciled.

global_invariant_source.scope: CON/NFR invariants below are checked against this source; ownership, state meaning, finance authority and success/failure gates are preserved per their linked source records and task constraints.

global_invariants.rule: Retryable commands/events and business side effects must remain idempotent; multi-path selection cannot create duplicate effects.
global_invariants.applicability: Where the path permits retries, replay, or business side effects.

global_invariants.rule: Tenant identity and institution isolation remain enforced; a path selector cannot trust a client-supplied tenant identity.
global_invariants.applicability: Every tenant/institution-scoped API, event, query, or selector.

global_invariants.rule: Sensitive operations retain tamper-evident audit coverage with actor, action, target, timestamp and outcome; selection does not replace execution evidence.
global_invariants.applicability: Sensitive operations and any selection/change operation in scope.

global_invariants.rule: Payment paths cannot store raw card data; provider capability and security controls remain separate gates.
Support-data access retains explicit consent/delegation, scope, time limitation and audit; a path choice cannot waive authorization.
Data ownership, state meanings, UNKNOWN handling, financial authority, and success/failure definitions are not changed by selecting a mode; unresolved items remain independently gated.

records.review_classification_raw: genuine owner/policy gate with narrow multi-path scope
records.rationale: The current registry contains exactly three active rows referencing ADR-004-GATE: REQ-PH02-OFFER-AND-VISIBILITY, SREQ-PH02-OFR-001, and SREQ-PH02-OFR-003; all are DRAFT. ADR-004's projection-only decision is already explicit and supported, and ODEC-002 confirms indicative display plus validate-and-reserve at checkout, so those resolved/sound portions must not receive multi-path treatment. The unresolved portion is the freshness threshold and stale/disconnected presentation. Sources explicitly allow hidden versus marked unavailable, and the Offer container lists re-query versus staleness warning for snapshots older than TTL. These form a narrow policy-selectable scope under one shared non-authoritative snapshot/checkout contract. No source supports selecting a different product-data owner, making ACCSystem authoritative, bypassing ACCore reservation, or inventing numeric freshness behavior; those remain excluded and/or blocked.

multi_path_scopes.source_scope: Stale price/availability snapshot presentation and institution-disconnected visibility only; do not reopen the resolved projection-vs-live-query architecture or the resolved checkout revalidation/reservation rule.
multi_path_scopes.selection_context: A later owner-approved policy selector chooses the stale/disconnected presentation/revalidation behavior and supplies the staleness threshold/TTL as a policy value. No numeric value, default mode, institution status code, or final API enum is asserted. Selection must not change source-of-truth ownership or permit checkout from a stale snapshot.
multi_path_scopes.shared_contract: ACCSystem exposes indicative marketplace price and availability snapshots with last_updated_at/staleness metadata; the projection is not authoritative, ACCore remains authoritative for product/inventory, stale/disconnected status is represented through the selected visibility outcome, and checkout must revalidate current price and quantity at ACCore and create an atomic reservation before authorization. The exact field names/types remain subject to the formal interface contract.

records.rationale: The current registry contains exactly four active rows whose open_decisions field includes ADR-006-GATE. The exact gate meaning in both affected requirement documents is only the unknown reservation hold TTL, not the reservation ownership, atomicity, UNKNOWN handling, or delivery mode. ADR-018 records the technical baseline that TTL is enforced by ACCore local policy and that the request TTL is only a hint; ADR-022 assigns the threshold to an institution-scoped, versioned policy store with Operations/SRE plus Finance ownership and explicit approval. This is an unresolved owner/policy gate, not a choice among multiple valid operational or implementation paths. ADR-006’s synchronous default and institution-approved callback option are a separate delivery-mode scope under ADR-015/ADR-018, and the source does not define multiple coexisting TTL implementations suitable for a shared contract and later selector. Therefore no multi-path treatment is applied. Existing semantics and invariants remain: ACCore is the inventory source of truth; reservation is local-transaction atomic and idempotent; elapsed time or timeout alone never proves expiry or authorizes release; UNKNOWN is reconciled before repeat effects; consumed/committed holds cannot be released; security/authentication and audit remain governed by their existing policies.

records.rationale: The current registry has 12 active rows carrying ADR-008-GATE. The canonical ADR explicitly settles only that Supervisor and Courier are frontend clients and CNT-ACC-DELIVERY owns authoritative delivery logic/state; it explicitly leaves online-only versus conditionally enabled queued interaction unselected. The offline requirement and courier container independently describe both source-supported operational paths and preserve the same invariants: client intent is non-authoritative, backend validation/acceptance is authoritative, replay is idempotent, conflicts are rejected/visible, and queue data is encrypted when approved. Therefore multi-path treatment is justified only for REQ-PH04-OFFLINE-COURIER-SYNC and its three sub-requirements. The other affected rows either reference provider-scope ownership/policy, POD compliance/policy, shipment/event contracts, or already-sound backend ownership and must not be broadened into invented alternatives.

multi_path_scopes.source_scope: Courier interaction/connectivity mode only: whether ACCMared Courier operates online-only or, when explicitly owner-approved, queues provisional offline status submissions for later synchronization. multi_path_scopes.selection_context: A later selector may choose online-only versus the conditionally enabled queued mode for the approved operational scope. multi_path_scopes.shared_contract: ACCMared Courier remains a thin client with no business logic; CNT-ACC-DELIVERY owns shipment records and authoritative delivery state. Both paths use the delivery API/backend validation boundary. A local display or queued record is provisional client intent only; only backend validation/acceptance changes authoritative state. Submission identity must support idempotent replay and the backend result is the reconciliation authority.

failure_recovery_audit_security: Offline queue entries are encrypted and survive process termination when the approved queued mode is enabled; local encryption key management remains UNKNOWN/owner-gated.
On reconnect, queued submissions use idempotent HTTP PATCH-style synchronization with exponential backoff and jitter; replay must not create duplicate authoritative state changes.
Fatal validation errors are surfaced to the courier; an offline update conflicting with current backend state is rejected visibly, and backend state wins rather than being overwritten by local state.
CNT-ACC-DELIVERY alone validates and commits authoritative delivery transitions and logs delivery operations through CNT-ACC-AUDIT; the client does not commit authoritative state.

Courier access is scoped to assigned shipments and supervisor access to the fleet in the delivery source, but those access statements are marked ASSUMPTION; short-lived tokens, secure storage, and no embedded mobile service secrets are source-supported security constraints.

No financial authority or financial state transition is specified in ADR-008 or the relevant courier/delivery requirements; therefore no financial behavior is asserted, and this review does not infer one.
separate_gates: Delivery-provider scope (platform fleet only versus external logistics integration) remains ODEC-010/UNKN-004/ASSUM-006 and an OWNER_UNASSIGNED decision; it affects delivery enablement and adapter design and is not resolved by the offline selector.

POD exact fields, privacy, retention, and compliance/data-residency policy remain UNKN-002/RGAP-PH04-004 and are not selectable paths under ADR-008-GATE.

Delivery API/schema/function evidence remains incomplete (RGAP-PH04-001, RGAP-PH04-002, RGAP-PH03-002); the affected requirements explicitly record NOT SPECIFIED contract references and planned verification only.

Shipment creation and external-event normalization retain their own source/gap and provider-scope dependencies; the backend ownership decision is already stated and must not be converted into a second implementation path.
Offline duration limits, eligible queued operations, local protection/retention details, retry/conflict policy details beyond the stated invariants, and owner approval records are not evidenced.

records.review_classification_raw: genuine owner/policy/security gate with unresolved approval-flow and session-TTL semantics; multi-path treatment does not apply
records.rationale: The current registry marks the nine listed IDs as active and associates ADR-011-GATE with them; no matching row is retired. The exact ADR-011 open scope is narrower than all access behavior: least privilege, MFA, scoped sessions, auditability, fail-closed identity behavior, token revocation, and separation of license entitlement from permission are already stated as baselines and should not be reclassified as selectable paths. ADR-011 explicitly selects the principle of least privilege plus approval plus scoped sessions plus full audit, but leaves the high-risk operation list and exact approval workflow UNKNOWN. The session sources state that revocation and short-lived tokens are required while the actual session TTL is UNKNOWN; no two or more concrete implementation or operational alternatives are specified. CNT-ACC-PLATFORMADMIN only records that the workflow engine or state machine is UNKNOWN and that unavailable approval leaves grants pending. Therefore there is no source-supported set of coexisting paths to place behind a shared contract and later selector. The correct treatment is to preserve the owner/policy/security gate and the separately documented consent, contract, and evidence gaps without inventing paths, statuses, values, approvals, or IDs.

remaining_blockers: ADR-011 approval flow / 4-eyes semantics are not defined; ADR-011 labels the 4-eyes principle an assumption and leaves the exact approval flow UNKNOWN.
Session TTL policy keys are required to be configurable, but no duration or approved value is asserted; the identity/session sources mark session TTL UNKNOWN and owner-unassigned.

For SREQ-PH01-SUP-002, the consent/delegation model is independently unresolved: per-session consent versus pre-authorized delegation remains under UNKN-008 and ODEC-013; ADR-011-GATE does not select between them.

The requirements and component sources identify missing interface/contract details for platform user lifecycle, role grants and support-session operations (RGAP-PH01-003); this is a traceability/source gap separate from ADR-011-GATE.
Formal owner/security approval and planned verification remain outstanding; repository evidence does not establish stakeholder approval, implementation, or production readiness.

records.rationale: The source explicitly names multiple coexisting transport/channel mechanisms (polling, long-polling, persistent channel, and optional protected inbound) and two authentication mechanisms (OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials and mTLS), while requiring one logical contract and policy-based per-institution selection. Therefore multi-path treatment is justified only for those narrow selectable sub-scopes. The same ADR separately states release trust requirements and planned verification; those are obligations and gates, not alternative implementation paths. Registry status confirms nine active DRAFT requirement IDs reference ADR-015-GATE, while the one matching retired requirement is excluded. No approval, numeric value, schema, runtime behavior, or evidence was inferred.

multi_path_scopes.source_scope: ACCSystem-ACCore connector transport/channel selection for firewalled institutions, narrowly scoped to SREQ-PH01-CONN-002 and the connectivity portion of REQ-PH01-CORE-CONNECTIVITY
multi_path_scopes.selection_context: Select per institution through operations/security/owner-approved policy based on firewall/reachability and deployment conditions. Outbound initiation is the proposed default for firewalled institutions; protected inbound is optional and approval-gated. The exact transport, query endpoint, callback mode/schema, channel parameters, and availability remain open.
multi_path_scopes.shared_contract: One logical authenticated ACCore connector contract with identical semantics across approved modes; Outbox/Inbox, at-least-once delivery, scoped idempotency and correlation, institution binding, and no direct database access. Logical event direction is not changed by protected inbound transport.

records.rationale: The current registry has exactly 12 non-retired rows whose open_decisions contain ADR-016-GATE. ADR-016 and the canonical payment/ledger sources explicitly retain multiple compatible operational paths: aggregated versus separate provider attempts, authorize-then-capture versus approved immediate capture, direct seller credit versus controlled central settlement, and externally completed/manual payment recording. These are suitable for a shared contract with a later selector because the sources define common allocation, state, idempotency, reconciliation, ledger and audit invariants. The selector must remain narrow and evidence-driven. ADR-016-GATE itself is not resolved: provider capability, commercial, owner, Finance/Legal/institution approval, settlement ownership, report contracts and manual-payment workflow remain blockers. The multi-seller ParentOrder/SellerOrder model is owner direction recorded in ADR-016 and is not treated as a new multi-path decision here; retired rows and unaffected order requirements are excluded.

ADR-018 records the UNKNOWN-safe rule and canonical vocabulary as a technical baseline, so those resolved semantics must not receive multi-path treatment. It explicitly documents two operationally valid reservation response modalities—synchronous response by default and institution-configurable async callback—so only delivery mode is suitable for a shared contract and later selector. multi_path_scopes.source_scope: Reservation response delivery between the order/integration path and ACCore: only transport/delivery modality is selector-controlled; UNKNOWN handling, expiry authority, vocabulary, payment gate, compensation guards, and state/idempotency invariants are fixed.
multi_path_scopes.selection_context: Select per institution through explicit ADR-015 connectivity configuration and onboarding policy. Synchronous is default; async callback requires named-institution approval and must not change state semantics or safety guards. No source supports an automatic runtime selector or universal async default.
multi_path_scopes.shared_contract: Both paths use the same reservation request and stable scoped idempotency key, ACCore as inventory/outcome authority, canonical statuses ACCEPTED, REJECTED, UNKNOWN and authoritative EXPIRED, durable saga/relay state, query or reconciliation by reservation_id and/or idempotency_key where an agreed channel exists, and identical response semantics. UNKNOWN is non-terminal; it blocks payment and never authorizes release, void, refund, compensation, or repeat effect. Elapsed time and reservation_ttl_seconds are not proof of expiry.
source_acceptance_criteria: Timeout/lost response becomes UNKNOWN, not REJECTED, blocks payment, records a query attempt, and causes no compensation or release.
Trusted query or authoritative callback resolving UNKNOWN to ACCEPTED does not repeat the reservation effect and permits payment only after every required hold and guard is satisfied.
A hold becomes EXPIRED only on authoritative ACCore evidence; local elapsed time and reservation_ttl_seconds alone never expire or release it.
Contract tests accept only ACCEPTED, REJECTED, UNKNOWN, and EXPIRED; RESERVED maps to ACCEPTED and INSUFFICIENT maps to REJECTED.
Definitive rejection/expiry compensates only eligible confirmed peer effects; unknown, consumed, committed, or ineligible reservations are not released.
Repeated requests, retries, duplicate responses, and callback redelivery use the same scoped idempotency identity and produce no duplicate reservation, release, payment, or compensation effect.

Both configured delivery modes preserve the same state machine, authority, authorization, audit, and reconciliation behavior; selected mode is evidenced in onboarding/configuration and contract tests.

failure_recovery_audit_security: Timeout, interruption, circuit-open after possible dispatch, or lost response on either path persists UNKNOWN, preserves the same idempotency key, blocks payment, and queries/reconciles by stable key or known reservation ID when supported; otherwise it waits safely and escalates.

Saga and relay persist state before external commands and use Outbox/Inbox and idempotent processing so restart, redelivery, or callback duplication cannot repeat effects.
ACCore performs the atomic inventory decision and remains source of truth; cross-institution writes are rejected and reserve/query/release/commit actions are audited.

Unresolved UNKNOWN retains evidence, moves to review/escalation, alerts Operations/SRE, and receives no automated compensation.

multi_path_scopes.source_scope: Institution-local ACCore financial journal trigger only; do not broaden this to ACCSystem confirmation atomicity, recipient projection, inventory commitment, software-license issuance, settlement ownership, or a universal journal trigger.
multi_path_scopes.selection_context: An institution-scoped accounting-trigger policy in the policy store selects the trigger event and point: OrderConfirmed receipt or a later configured event. Selection requires explicit Finance owner approval and the ADR states no production financial-journal activation without explicit Finance/Legal/Compliance owner approval. The architecture provides the event and hook; the institution declares the commitment point.
multi_path_scopes.shared_contract: OrderConfirmed is an ACCSystem operational state transition and delivery-unlock signal, not a universal journal-posting instruction. ACCSystem emits the event only after all required reservations are accepted, payment is definitive for the approved mode, and the immutable snapshot, CONFIRMED state, and outbox record commit atomically. The event carries the order and seller-order references, payment reference(s), policy_snapshot_version, confirmed_at, line_items, and institution_id; it does not carry a journal_entry instruction. ACCore consumes the event and applies an institution-local accounting policy, with the journal entry governed by the institution's Finance function, jurisdiction, accounting standard, and revenue-recognition rules. Ledger entries remain subject to the referenced append-only ADR-016 requirements regardless of trigger timing.

records.rationale: The current requirements registry marks exactly eight active DRAFT rows with ADR-021-GATE. ADR-021 is an interim, approval-required policy: it records URI-path major versioning as a candidate proposal, while listing header-based versioning as an alternative considered, no-versioning as unacceptable, and exposed semantic minor versions as overkill; it does not approve these as coexisting selectable runtime or implementation paths. Its change-later mechanism explicitly requires a new ADR and formal API Governance approval to change URI versus header strategy, and its assumptions state that no interface has an approved major-version mapping. The interface contract source independently says versioning remains PROPOSED/UNKNOWN/OWNER-REVIEW-REQUIRED and that every illustrative v1/path value is unassigned. Therefore this is not a resolved decision and not a sound multi-path contract with a later selector. The connectivity modes, authentication choices, retry/DLQ behavior, and order-aggregate paths documented elsewhere are separate concerns governed by ADR-015, ADR-022, IC-004, ODEC-003, and related gaps; attributing them to ADR-021 would broaden the reference beyond its source-supported scope. No multi-path scope is recorded.

Broker events, provider-owned webhooks, connector delivery, and other non-HTTP or externally controlled contracts require their own approved schema/version treatment; ADR-021 asserts no universal transport version.
The affected requirement documents retain planned verification only; no implementation, execution evidence, or stakeholder approval is claimed.

records.rationale: The current registry links ASSUM-003 to exactly REQ-PH03-PAYMENT-ORCHESTRATION and SREQ-PH03-PAY-002. ASSUM-003 is not resolved: it states a single MVP provider and asks for Phase 3 confirmation. However, the affected payment-allocation scope already documents multiple valid operational paths that can coexist behind a shared internal contract and later selector: compatible aggregate provider transaction versus separate SellerOrder attempts. The sources explicitly preserve those alternatives, define the compatibility/provider-capability selector, and require separate attempts or blocking when aggregation is not supported. This does not justify inventing a multi-provider fallback, choosing a provider, or closing the owner/Finance/Legal gates. The treatment is therefore narrow and preserves all unrelated payment, settlement, policy, security, compliance, and evidence blockers.

multi_path_scopes.shared_contract: Create exactly one durable payment allocation per SellerOrder containing seller, SellerOrder/order scope, amount, currency, tax/delivery basis, policy snapshot or capture-policy ID, correlation ID, payment-attempt identity, and operation-scoped idempotency key. Route provider-specific translation through CMP-PAY-ADAPTER and keep provider references tied to allocation/payment_attempt/SellerOrder scope; never infer allocation from order_id alone. Unsupported provider capabilities are explicit errors/deferred states and the affected path is blocked, not assumed.

failure_recovery_audit_security: Provider timeout, ambiguous status, 5xx, or circuit-open after possible dispatch is UNKNOWN unless durable evidence proves non-dispatch; reconcile provider state before retry, void, capture, compensation, or release.

Retries reuse the scoped operation idempotency key and must not create a second authorization/capture or duplicate financial effect; duplicate webhook receipt is durably deduplicated by provider event/operation scope.
A failed or unsupported aggregate path must not be silently collapsed into another mode; use separate attempts or block/defer according to policy and capability evidence.
AUTHORIZED remains a hold, CAPTURED remains collection, and neither alone establishes seller credit or settlement; seller credit/transfer and settlement remain separate reconciliation states.

Payment records and ledger postings are append-only/idempotent with source reference, currency, amount, actor, correlation, policy snapshot, reversal/duplicate linkage, and reconciliation evidence; corrections use reversal/adjustment rather than mutation.

Inbound webhooks require signature validation before state mutation, invalid signatures raise a security alert, outbound provider calls use TLS, credentials/secrets stay in an external secret store, and raw PAN/CVV/expiry never enter ACCSystem stores.

The eventual approved contract must define explicit per-interface version/schema mappings, compatibility rules, consumer behavior, and deprecation/sunset records through API Governance; non-HTTP, broker, provider-owned webhook, and connector-delivery contracts require their own approved schema/version treatment rather than an invented universal transport version.

During compatibility or migration, prior contracts remain retained until the approved deprecation window/sunset conditions are met; consumers must tolerate unknown error codes, and extensible enum additions require documented unknown-value behavior.

Connector interruption queues messages in the Outbox; it is not treated as rejection. Delivery uses the documented Outbox/Inbox, at-least-once, stable idempotency-key and deduplication baseline, with retry/recovery governed by approved policy.
Integration failures, schema/signature failures, and security events are logged by the Integration Gateway/integration audit path; invalid signatures or schema are rejected structurally and alerted.

Every message remains bound to the authenticated institution; transport is TLS and service authentication is the ADR-015 policy-selected OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials or mTLS method. No direct ACCore database access is permitted.

failure_recovery_audit_security: Preserve local outbox/inbox state, delivery state and the original idempotency key across dispatch uncertainty; local dispatch failure is not proof of non-delivery.
Retry using the same idempotency key; duplicate completed effects must not repeat business effects, and in-progress/uncertain work must be recovered or reconciled rather than blindly re-executed.
DLQ is a delivery condition, not a business rejection or completion. Before replaying a financial or reservation command, query the source of truth by idempotency key.
Per-key/per-aggregate ordering is supported only where configured; consumers retain version/order guards. Global ordering and cross-DLQ ordering are not implied.
A committed Catalog write whose relay fails retains durable intent and is retried or reconciled without claiming downstream completion; retries/DLQ must not duplicate listing effects.
Order transition history and its outbox event remain atomically persisted under optimistic concurrency; concurrent transition attempts must not both succeed.
Producer publication and consumer subscription require authorization. Specific ACL design, retention and security approval are not supplied by the sources.

Recovery, compensation, reconciliation and relevant effects remain auditable; retention must not delete records needed for deduplication, reconciliation or audit. No numeric retry, backoff, timeout or retention value is asserted.

records.rationale: The current requirements and canonical sources consistently define one shared TTL semantic: ACCore enforces a configurable local hold policy; the reservation request may carry only a hint; and expiry is accepted only from authoritative ACCore evidence. ADR-018 records the technical baseline and explicitly leaves numeric TTL values configurable per institution and approval-required. ADR-022 specifies the policy registry, owner functions (Operations/SRE plus Finance), versioned approval, and fail-closed behavior when no approved value exists. Because the open portion is a missing owner-approved policy value rather than two or more source-supported coexisting operational or implementation paths, multi-path treatment would invent alternatives and is not applicable. The sound UNKNOWN/expiry, idempotency, reconciliation, financial-safety, and audit-related rules remain unchanged; no new contract or selector is proposed.
remaining_blockers: The authoritative reservation hold TTL numeric value remains UNKNOWN and requires institution-specific approval by the Operations/SRE and Finance owners under ADR-022 before production activation.
The request-side reservation_ttl_seconds value remains a non-authoritative hint; ACCore local policy is the only authority and the saga must not infer expiry from elapsed wall-clock time.
ADR-006-GATE remains a related policy gate for reservation hold TTL and ADR-022-GATE remains an owner-approval gate; these are not alternative implementation paths.
IC-006 is a separate delivery-mode contract gate for synchronous response versus approved asynchronous callback and is outside IC-005's TTL scope.

Canonical sources explicitly state synchronous response as the default and asynchronous callback as a configurable per-institution option, so these are valid coexisting paths suitable for one shared contract and later selector. ADR-018 simultaneously fixes the non-selectable semantics: UNKNOWN-safe handling, canonical statuses, ACCore authority, no unsafe retry/release/financial effect, and authoritative reconciliation. Therefore only delivery modality receives multi-path treatment; unresolved query/channel/schema/TTL/approval issues remain separate blockers rather than being inferred or folded into the selector.

An ACCEPTED outcome carries the reservation reference when known, confirmed price, confirmed quantity, and expiry-policy reference; the stable scoped idempotency/request key is persisted before dispatch and remains the correlation/reconciliation key. ACCore remains inventory source of truth; the response/notification path must not change the outcome meaning or permit a second reservation effect.

records.rationale: IC-007 is not resolved by the proposed interface/security descriptions. The requirement document explicitly records anonymous browsing as an open security decision and maps it to SREQ-PH02-DSC-001; the current registry maps the same decision to the parent REQ-PH02-PRODUCT-DISCOVERY and child SREQ-PH02-DSC-001. The interface contract marks public catalog access as UNKNOWN and requiring an explicit security policy decision, while the security view presents anonymous browsing as a possible public permission model but is itself PROPOSED and not an approval record. The decision is therefore an owner/policy/security gate, not a choice among multiple valid coexisting operational or implementation paths. No multi-path treatment is warranted: permitting versus denying anonymous access are mutually exclusive policy outcomes, and the sources do not define a selector, shared contract, path-specific recovery, or reconciliation behavior for them. Existing catalog invariants remain applicable regardless of the eventual policy: the catalog returns marketplace projections rather than product-master data; institution-scoped reads enforce the verified institution/tenant claim; search is derived/rebuildable and is not the source of listing truth; and catalog snapshots are not checkout authority. These are not IC-007 resolutions and were not expanded into invented acceptance criteria.
remaining_blockers: IC-007 remains an explicit unresolved security/policy decision: whether unauthenticated catalog browsing is permitted; no owner, approval, or final status is recorded.
IC-002 remains separately open for SREQ-PH02-DSC-001: exact field names/types require formal OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification.
PUB-004 remains separately open on the parent requirement's multilingual listing-field sub-scope: permitted publication fields are undefined.
The parent and sub-requirement are DRAFT, with planned rather than executed verification; the registry and strict-ready ledger retain IC-007 on exactly these two active rows.

records.rationale: The current requirements registry contains IC-008 only on REQ-PH01-LICENSE-VALIDATION and SREQ-PH01-LICV-004; the other registry row with the same broad license area, SREQ-PH01-LIC-008, does not cite IC-008 and must not be added. The canonical requirement says expired offline credentials restrict licensed functions unless an applicable grace policy is approved, and its acceptance criterion says no grace applies unless approved; it does not define a second approved behavior, a duration, or a selector. The interface contract and CMP-CON-LICENSECHECK likewise specify the fail-closed/restrictive behavior absent an approved applicable grace policy, while marking grace behavior and duration UNKNOWN. ADR-014 identifies signed-token offline validation as PROPOSED and separately records grace as an UNKNOWN policy value owned by an unassigned owner. Therefore IC-008 is a missing owner-approved policy/security value, not a pair of source-supported coexisting implementation paths. Online validation versus local signed-token validation are already separate paths in the broader contract, but their existence does not make grace duration multi-path-selectable, and the broader ODEC-014 strategy gate must remain distinct.
remaining_blockers: UNKN-003: license model granularity, renewal cycle, and grace-period duration remain undefined; the registry links this to the parent validation requirement and SREQ-PH01-LICV-004.
UNKN-009: offline-validation strategy and grace period remain undefined.
ODEC-008: ACCore offline behavior scope, including which modules operate offline and for how long, remains open.
ODEC-014: signed short-lived token versus mandatory periodic connectivity is a broader offline-validation strategy decision; it is not resolved by IC-008 and must remain separate.
LIC-001: entitlement TTL and grace-period duration remain open; TTL and grace affect revocation exposure and connectivity resilience.
The affected requirement is OWNER_REVIEW and its verification is planned only; no executed evidence or approval is present.

records.rationale: The active registry links LIC-001 to the lifecycle main requirement, LIC-009, LIC-010, the validation main requirement, LICV-003, and LICV-004; retired LIC-001 and LIC-004 source rows are not treated as active requirements. Canonical sources explicitly define two coexisting validation paths—offline signed-token verification and online validation/fallback—with a shared read-only, scoped result contract and documented failure behavior. They do not support inventing a third implementation, selecting TTL/grace values, or treating ADR-014's rejected alternatives as coequal paths. Therefore multi-path treatment is appropriate only for runtime validation-path selection, while TTL/grace and all lifecycle/audit/revocation gates remain unresolved.

multi_path_scopes.source_scope: Offline tolerance behavior for institutional license validation: execution-path selection after a valid locally held credential is unavailable or expired. This scope covers the already documented online and offline validation paths; it does not make TTL, grace duration, lifecycle state transitions, audit obligations, or terminal revocation selector-controlled.
multi_path_scopes.selection_context: Selector scope is limited to runtime availability and credential state: use offline validation when a locally held signed credential and usable public key are available; use online validation when no valid offline credential is held or an expired credential can be checked online; when the credential is expired and no network is available, return EXPIRED_OFFLINE and apply only an explicitly approved grace policy, otherwise restrict/fail closed. Exact token TTL and grace duration are policy values under LIC-001 and are not selected by this review.
multi_path_scopes.shared_contract: Both paths implement FN-LIC-VALIDATE for a workflow-scoped entitlement result. The result keeps lifecycle status distinct from evaluation verdict and may represent VALID, INVALID, EXPIRED_OFFLINE, suspended, revoked, not-found, over-capacity, or unresolved policy/availability as applicable. Validation is read-only; token issuance/refresh is separate. The contract is institutional {institution_id, product_code} in PH-01, with no ERP data in request or response.

failure_recovery_audit_security: Fixed state invariant: validation does not change license/business state; online validation reads entitlement state, and token issuance/refresh is not a validation side effect.
Fixed idempotency invariant: validation is a read-only query and inherently idempotent; issuance/refresh has separate retriable semantics.

Fixed financial authority invariant: these sources define entitlement validation/gating only; no financial, accounting, billing, or ERP mutation authority is granted to either path, and separately permitted local ERP operation remains unharmed.

Fixed security invariant: invalid signature, missing key, mismatched workflow/identity/scope, or absent/unverifiable required grant evidence never yields VALID or token-derived grace; the private signing key remains in ACCSystem and ACCore uses public-key verification only.

Fixed fail-closed invariant: expired offline credentials without an available online result restrict licensed functions unless an approved applicable grace policy exists; local ERP operation that is separately permitted continues.

Failure/recovery: online database or connectivity failure returns an error or uses a valid cached/offline credential where documented; expired offline credentials use online fallback when available; signing/token refresh failure remains durable and retriable and does not claim readiness before successful signing.

Reconciliation/observability: online validation telemetry and failed-validation security audit logging are documented, while high-volume audit rate/selection remains an explicit assumption; invalid-token anomalies are logged without the full token. License lifecycle state changes remain actor/reason/timestamp/institution/product audited under SREQ-PH01-LIC-009, independent of which validation path was used.

multi_path_scopes.shared_contract: All paths preserve the same license identity and lifecycle meaning: a revocation/suspension is a license-owned state outcome, ACCore must not report an unresolved or invalid credential as VALID, licensed functions are restricted for a known negative or expired-offline result unless an applicable grace policy is explicitly approved, and independently permitted local ERP operation remains available. The contract must carry authenticated institutional scope and product/license identity; exact event fields, mapping, transport version, receiver/ACK semantics, and numeric propagation timing are not specified by the sources.

failure_recovery_audit_security: State invariant: a revoked license never returns to Active; a LicenseSuspended result/event restricts the licensed module; online and offline lifecycle status/evaluation must not be conflated.

Idempotency/integrity invariant: event delivery is at-least-once with possible duplicates; consumers use Inbox/processed-message handling, and immutable events require a new event or explicit compensation for correction. The lifecycle transition is published once per idempotent transition in the dynamic flow.

Failure/recovery: if online validation is unavailable, ACCore may fall back to a valid scoped cached/signed credential; if the credential is expired offline or online fallback is unavailable, licensed functions are restricted unless an applicable grace policy is approved. No token-derived access is granted for invalid signature, missing key, wrong scope, or absent required grant evidence.

Security invariant: ACCore receives/uses only the platform public key; the signing private key remains in ACCSystem. Validation must be authenticated and institution-scoped, must not request or expose ERP data, and invalid/tampered credentials fail closed and are logged with token metadata without the full token.

records.rationale: The active registry contains exactly four rows referencing LIC-005: the two parent requirements and the two active sub-requirements SREQ-PH01-LIC-002 and SREQ-PH01-LICV-006. The retired SREQ-PH01-LIC-005 is excluded because it is not active and its LIC-005 association was removed in the decomposition. Sources establish one selected cryptographic mechanism: ACCSystem retains the private key, distributes a public key to ACCore, validators accept the active key set, and during rotation both old and new keys are valid during an overlap. They also establish one validation fallback behavior: local verification tries all current valid keys and returns INVALID if none verify. However, sources do not establish two or more selectable/coexisting key-propagation implementations. Config file/certificate store, provisioning distribution, and an operational distribution procedure are described as storage/operational references or unknown procedure—not as separately valid paths with defined contracts. Online validation is a validation fallback, not a documented public-key rotation propagation path. Therefore no shared-contract/selector treatment is applied. The open sub-scope remains a genuine Architecture/Security owner gate and unresolved operational semantics. Source-supported acceptance remains: after rotation, new-key tokens verify; tampered payloads fail; invalid signature, missing key, or mismatched identity never yields VALID; private key never reaches ACCore; validators use the active key set; and failure to verify returns INVALID. These do not close the distribution procedure or approval gate.

Therefore no shared contract, selector, path failure/recovery/reconciliation behavior, or new multi-path treatment can be derived without inventing policy, ownership, or interface decisions. source_acceptance_criteria: A multi-seller cart creates exactly one ParentOrder and one SellerOrder per seller with no cross-seller line mixing.
For a validated checkout, ParentOrder, all SellerOrders, and corresponding SellerOrderCreated outbox records persist in one local transaction; a pre-commit failure leaves none committed.
A repeated or concurrent split for the same validated checkout returns the existing ParentOrder/SellerOrders and creates no duplicate order or outbox records.
Payment is not requested until all required reservations are definitively accepted.
The aggregation path is used only with compatible seller policies and provider support; otherwise separate per-SellerOrder attempts are used or checkout is blocked by policy.
Payment timeout yields PaymentUnknown with no duplicate financial effect; reservation timeout yields UNKNOWN with no payment or unsafe release.
Authorize-then-capture and immediate capture remain separately testable where approved/supported, and capture, seller credit, and settlement remain distinct states.
Saga restart and outbox relay recovery resume persisted state without duplicate holds, payments, confirmations, or outbox events.

failure_recovery_audit_security: Payment is not eligible until every required SellerOrder reservation is definitively ACCEPTED; REJECTED/authoritatively EXPIRED blocks checkout and UNKNOWN blocks payment and unsafe release.
Reservation/payment timeouts or lost responses remain UNKNOWN and require query/reconciliation; retries use stable scoped idempotency keys and never create duplicate holds or financial effects.

Definitive payment failure requires reconciliation of peer reservations/payment effects and compensation only for eligible known effects under the applicable guard; unresolved compensation remains pending/review and prevents closure.

Local aggregate, SellerOrders, and SellerOrderCreated outbox records commit atomically or not at all; replay/concurrent retry returns existing records without duplicates; outbox delivery failure is retried without rolling back the committed order.

Each payment/ledger posting is auditable with stable idempotency key, source reference, currency, amount, actor, and reversal/duplicate linkage; manual payment requires institution-scoped permission, reason, evidence reference, and approval workflow.

Unknown or failed downstream effects do not implicitly roll back ParentOrder, mark failure, release an unknown hold, or repeat a financial action; recovery resumes persisted saga state with at-least-once/idempotent operations.

records.rationale: ODEC-005 is not resolved and is not merely a traceability gap: canonical sources explicitly define two valid, seller/agreement-selected operational paths and explicitly require a shared allocation/attempt contract with split-or-block behavior for incompatible policies. Therefore multi-path treatment is justified narrowly for SREQ-PH03-PAY-003. The parent requirement is affected because its registry open_decisions includes ODEC-005, but no broad parent-level closure is warranted. The paths, selector, state distinctions, UNKNOWN-safe recovery, idempotency, audit, ledger, security, and acceptance rules above are directly source-supported; unresolved owner, provider, finance/legal, compliance, and interface-contract gates are preserved.

multi_path_scopes.source_scope: Capture-policy selection for SREQ-PH03-PAY-003 only: per-SellerOrder seller/agreement capture timing. ODEC-005 does not resolve the parent requirement's other reservation, provider, settlement, security, or compliance boundaries.
multi_path_scopes.selection_context: The policy resolver selects AUTHORIZE_THEN_CAPTURE or IMMEDIATE_CAPTURE per seller/agreement using approved platform, provider, risk, legal, finance, and institutional policy/configuration. For incompatible policies in one transaction, select separate attempts or block checkout; never silently choose one policy. No provider, numeric value, or approval is inferred.
multi_path_scopes.shared_contract: For every SellerOrder, create one payment allocation containing seller, SellerOrder/order, amount, currency, tax/delivery basis, capture-policy snapshot/ID, correlation ID, and operation-specific idempotency key. The policy resolver selects exactly one approved mode per seller/agreement; AUTHORIZED is a reversible hold, CAPTURED is collection, and neither state proves seller credit or settlement. A shared aggregate provider transaction is permitted only when seller policies are compatible and provider seller-allocation support exists; otherwise use separate attempts or block checkout. Raw card data is never stored.
source_acceptance_criteria: With any reservation UNKNOWN, REJECTED, or EXPIRED, no payment request is issued.

Each allocation contains the required seller, amount, currency, tax/delivery basis, policy snapshot, correlation, and idempotency fields; aggregate use occurs only for compatible policies with provider support.

Both authorize-then-capture and immediate-capture state paths are tested per SellerOrder, including compatible aggregation where supported.
Retries use the same operation key and produce no second authorization or capture; provider timeout, duplicate webhook, and later definitive evidence are reconciled.
Capture failure after confirmation leaves the order visible/confirmed with a payment exception; no silent completion.
Ledger postings are balanced, immutable, and idempotent; seller-credit mismatch, commission posting, reversal/refund/void eligibility, and reconciliation are verified; no raw card data is found.

failure_recovery_audit_security: Payment cannot start until every required SellerOrder reservation is definitively ACCEPTED; UNKNOWN, REJECTED, or EXPIRED reservation blocks payment.

Timeout or lost provider response becomes AUTHORIZATION_UNKNOWN or CAPTURE_UNKNOWN; it is not treated as failure, and no duplicate financial effect, release, void, retry, or compensation occurs until authoritative provider evidence/reconciliation resolves it.

Definitive failure blocks confirmation, reconciles in-flight attempts/reservations, and compensates only eligible known effects under the applicable guards; capture failure after confirmation leaves the order confirmed with a visible payment exception and retry/reconciliation/void/refund handling.

Every payment operation uses scoped, operation-specific idempotency identity; duplicate webhook/retry produces no duplicate authorization or capture. Provider references, order/SellerOrder, allocation, amount, currency, policy snapshot, actor/source, correlation, reversal/duplicate links, and reconciliation evidence are retained.

Payment and ledger records are append-only/idempotent; corrections use reversal/adjustment postings. AUTHORIZED, CAPTURED, seller credit/transfer, and settlement remain distinct states. Raw PAN/CVV/expiry are excluded. Unsupported provider capabilities are explicit errors or deferred/blocked states.

records.rationale: ODEC-007 is an unresolved semantic/design boundary, not a resolved decision and not a source-supported multi-path choice. The canonical scope table states 'Returns and disputes capability' with 'Returns domain design pending' for Phase 6. The PH-03 documents explicitly defer return/dispute handling and partial-refund policy, while the PH-04 document explicitly leaves return-to-sender, re-attempt, recipient-absent, and delivery-failure behavior undefined. Therefore no valid_paths, shared contract, selector, or path-specific recovery/reconciliation contract can be truthfully listed without inventing behavior. The already-defined cancellation/payment invariants remain applicable: authoritative payment/reservation state, void only for uncaptured authorization, refund only for captured funds, scoped idempotency, no over-refund, UNKNOWN reconciliation before compensation, explicit partial outcomes, and cancellation halting delivery; these are not ODEC-007 paths. The active registry rows directly carrying ODEC-007 are the four listed affected IDs; SREQ-PH03-VRF-003 is the only directly identified sub-requirement in its document and is included because the current active dependency record identifies it as ODEC-007-affected.

records.rationale: The current registry has exactly two non-retired rows containing ODEC-008: the parent institutional license-validation requirement and SREQ-PH01-LICV-004. ODEC-008 asks which ACCore modules operate offline and for how long. Canonical sources establish a general invariant—licensed functions fail closed/restrict unless an approved applicable grace policy exists, while separately permitted local ERP operations continue—but do not enumerate the offline-capable module set or choose a duration. The online REST and local signed-token validation paths are explicit source-supported paths, but they answer the separate ODEC-014 mechanism question and are already represented by FN-LIC-VALIDATE/ADR-014; they do not provide multiple ODEC-008 module/duration policies. Therefore no multi-path scope is recorded. The unresolved part is an owner/business/security policy and semantic scope gate, with planned—not executed—acceptance evidence. No approval, status promotion, numeric duration, or behavior beyond the cited sources is inferred.

records.rationale: The current requirements registry identifies exactly four active affected IDs: the two parent requirements and their active ODEC-009 sub-requirements; no retired child is included. Canonical requirements state ODEC-009 as 'Multi-currency and tax model/jurisdiction rules' and explicitly preserve it as open. The canonical policy register provides a governance baseline—versioned tax lines and exchange-rate snapshots configured by finance/tax and subject to jurisdiction review—and ADR-017 selects versioned, owner-approved policy snapshots while stating that legal/tax determination is an external gate. These sources define a governance direction and immutable historical snapshot behavior, not multiple valid coexisting operational or implementation paths for the unresolved tax/currency model. The documented ADR-017 alternatives (hard-coded values and independent per-service settings) are explicitly unsafe trade-offs, not source-supported selectable paths for this decision. Therefore no multi-path treatment is applied. The sound fixed invariants that remain applicable are: checkout must stop on invalid/changed price or quantity and refresh data; confirmed-order commercial terms include currency and tax; policy/rule versions used are retained; snapshots are authoritative, append-only, immutable, written atomically, idempotent, internally authorized, institution-isolated, auditable, and never replaced by current product data. These invariants do not invent the missing tax/currency semantics.

remaining_blockers: ODEC-009 remains unresolved: the source only states that the currency model and tax jurisdiction rules must be defined; it does not select a tax model, jurisdiction determination rule, exchange-rate authority, rounding/precision policy, or multi-currency conversion behavior.
Finance/tax jurisdiction review is an explicit gate for the tax/currency policy; ADR-017 also requires owner ratification of tax lines/rules and exchange-rate source. No approval is recorded.
UNKN-006 remains attached to both active sub-requirements, and PH-02 RGAP-PH02-009 records that tax-line, currency, and delivery-term snapshot content is undefined pending the model.

AC-PH02-CHK-003-02 and AC-PH03-ORD-006-01 remain source-reference/verification gaps; their verification is planned only. Exact API/event field schemas also remain unresolved where the cited interface text is proposal/assumption material.

The broad PH-03 parent also retains independent open decisions and gates (including ODEC-003, IC-002, ADR-021-GATE, ADR-018-GATE, IC-004, RGAP-PH02-004, and ADR-017-GATE); ODEC-009 does not resolve or replace them.

records.rationale: ODEC-010 names two source-supported, semantically compatible delivery execution choices: ACCMared's platform-owned fleet and external logistics-provider integration. The architecture deliberately preserves external versus ACCMared delivery as an alternative and requires a provider-agnostic boundary, so the narrow provider-selection sub-scope is suitable for a shared contract and later per-institution selector. However, the decision is not resolved: the registry and canonical sources retain ODEC-010/UNKN-004/ASSUM-006/ADR-008-GATE, owner review, missing contract/use-case evidence, and planned verification. Therefore the multi-path treatment documents the alternatives without inventing an approval, selector value, interface, or behavior.

records.rationale: The current requirements registry directly associates ODEC-011 with the active main requirement REQ-PH01-LICENSE-LIFECYCLE and active sub-requirements SREQ-PH01-LIC-007 and SREQ-PH01-LIC-008; the historical SREQ-PH01-LIC-001 is RETIRED and is excluded. The canonical lifecycle document states that ODEC-011 covers license type, granularity, renewal, and grace period, while its active requirements only establish rejection of ineligible or invalid requests and creation of an institution/product-bound ISSUED record. CMP-LIC-ISSUANCE explicitly says license type (per-institution, per-seat, or per-unit) depends on product configuration and is UNKNOWN; it does not establish selectable operational paths or a shared selector contract. The lifecycle document separately records grace behavior as OPEN and says no automatic grace is defined. The documented institutional and marketplace workflows are distinct scope workflows: marketplace post-purchase issuance is explicitly outside PH-01, and the lifecycle component says the workflows must not be conflated. That distinction is not evidence of multiple valid coexisting paths for the ODEC-011 institutional license-model decision. No source-supported path selector, path-specific recovery/reconciliation contract, or ODEC-011-specific acceptance criteria distinguishing alternatives exists. Therefore no multi-path treatment is justified. Existing source-supported invariants remain applicable without resolving ODEC-011: authorized eligibility/plan validation precedes issuance; failure creates no license record; success creates an institution/product-bound record in ISSUED; license entitlement is separate from user permissions; duplicate operations must not issue another license; issuance/state changes are auditable; and unresolved policy must not be invented.

records.rationale: The current registry has exactly three active rows carrying ODEC-014: REQ-PH01-LICENSE-VALIDATION, SREQ-PH01-LICV-003 and SREQ-PH01-LICV-004. Canonical sources document two coexisting operational validation paths—online institutional validation and offline local signed-token verification—with a source-defined selector and recovery behavior. Therefore a shared contract and later selector are justified only for that execution sub-scope. ODEC-014's stated alternatives are not both equally valid under the requirements: ADR-014 marks signed tokens as the selected proposed mechanism and states always-online validation breaks the offline-operation requirement. Treating mandatory periodic connectivity as a second implementation path would invent an allowed behavior. The open decision is consequently not resolved: the mechanism is only proposed, while TTL, grace, module/offline scope, key rotation and related policy/security ownership gates remain open. No multi-path treatment is applied to those gates or to already-sound read-only, scope, key-custody, fail-closed, and local-ERP invariants.

multi_path_scopes.source_scope: Institutional license validation for a scoped institution/product request, including connectivity loss and credential expiry; marketplace validation is explicitly outside this PH-01 requirement scope.
multi_path_scopes.selection_context: Use the offline path when ACCore has a valid scoped signed credential and can verify the platform key and required claims locally. If no valid offline credential is held, or the credential is expired and connectivity is available, use online validation. If the credential is expired and no network is available, return EXPIRED_OFFLINE and restrict/fail closed unless an explicitly approved applicable grace policy permits otherwise. Mandatory always-online validation is not listed as a coequal valid implementation path here because ADR-014 records that it breaks the stated offline-operation requirement; ADR-014 itself remains PROPOSED.
multi_path_scopes.shared_contract: Both paths validate the same institutional entitlement scope and return a scoped license outcome without ERP data; lifecycle status and evaluation result remain distinct; VALID requires the applicable signature/identity/grant/credential checks; validation is read-only and token issuance or refresh is a separate retriable license-owned operation.

failure_recovery_audit_security: State invariant: acceptance records durable accepted work, not final Catalog/search completion; Catalog state and its event trail evidence final processing separately.

Idempotency invariant: redelivery may occur; stable source event_id and the scoped institution_id/seller_product_id/version business key prevent duplicate listing or version effects. Completed duplicates may return an available recorded outcome; in-progress or uncertain duplicates require an approved safe status/retry/recovery contract, not a fabricated completion.

Recovery invariant: accepted Integration Inbox state and Catalog-delivery intent commit atomically within the Integration-local boundary; Catalog writes remain separately owned. Lost acknowledgments, crashes, Catalog unavailability, and event-relay failure retain/retry/reconcile durable work without claiming downstream completion.

Outbox invariant: ACCore marks the Outbox message SENT only on a contract-valid acceptance receipt; transient or uncertain delivery remains recoverable, and definitive pre-admission errors are retained for correction and resubmission.

Rejection invariant: definitive pre-admission validation or permission rejection records the rejected attempt and reason, returns structured non-success, creates no listing or Catalog delivery intent, and is auditable. The exact rejected-attempt wire/schema representation is still open.
Version/state invariant: a lower version than current has no listing-state mutation; listing_id remains stable across updates. Search lag or retry does not invalidate an accepted publication.

Security invariant: TLS and institution authentication/authorization remain required; the gateway validates the authenticated institution binding against the payload. The authentication method is the ADR-015-selected OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials or mTLS path and remains an onboarding/security approval gate.
Audit invariant: received, rejected, and processed publication outcomes are recorded in the documented audit/event records; no audit event is treated as a Catalog state-event alias.
Financial authority invariant: these PUB-005 sources specify no financial effect or financial authority for publication; do not add payment, ledger, or settlement behavior to either path.

records.rationale: The current requirements registry contains exactly two active rows that reference RGAP-PH02-004: SREQ-PH03-ORD-007 and SREQ-PH03-ORD-008. The PH-02 requirement explicitly records order-record placement as an owner gate and states that PH-02 carries only seller-scoped reservation subject identity, while PH-03 owns the order aggregate lifecycle. The canonical checkout function and multi-seller component describe one concrete sequence: validate and group the checkout, atomically persist ParentOrder, SellerOrders, saga state and outbox records, then start seller reservations. They do not document a second valid placement/implementation path for this gap, nor a shared contract and selector that could support coexisting modes. The cited alternative paths in ADR-016 are payment/provider alternatives and are outside RGAP-PH02-004; applying multi-path treatment to them would broaden the reference beyond its source-defined scope. The retired SREQ-PH03-ORD-001 is not an active affected requirement and is therefore excluded from affected_requirement_ids.
remaining_blockers: RGAP-PH02-004 itself remains unresolved: owner decision is required on placement of the pre-reservation ParentOrder/SellerOrder shell at the PH-02/PH-03 boundary.
SREQ-PH03-ORD-007 remains blocked by ODEC-003, IC-002, and ADR-021-GATE; its transaction atomicity verification is explicitly planned only.
SREQ-PH03-ORD-008 remains blocked by ODEC-003, IC-002, and ADR-021-GATE; its repeated/concurrent replay verification is explicitly planned only.

The order-create request/response shapes are marked assumptions requiring formal OpenAPI specification; interface versioning is proposed/approval-required, so no approved selector or schema contract exists.

multi_path_scopes.shared_contract: All paths use ACCEPTED, REJECTED, UNKNOWN and authoritative EXPIRED. Unknown release is reconciled before another release attempt.

Saga restart produces no duplicate reservations, payments, confirmations or outbox effects.

records.rationale: RP-02 is not resolved: the remediation plan explicitly requires an external security/operations decision, and the requirements registry marks the parent and both directly referenced sub-requirements DRAFT with RP-02 in open_decisions. The canonical sources independently document more than one valid deployment mode: outbound-initiated connectivity is the default for firewalled institutions, while protected inbound is optional where approved; outbound transport variants include polling, long-polling, and persistent channel. They also explicitly require one logical contract with identical semantics. Therefore multi-path treatment is justified only for SREQ-PH01-CONN-002. SREQ-PH01-CONN-006 is affected because interruption/recovery behavior depends operationally on the selected mode, but its required health-state and local-continuity behavior is a fixed cross-path contract and must not be treated as another unresolved selector. No approval, status, identifier, numeric value, or unrecorded behavior has been inferred.

multi_path_scopes.source_scope: Connectivity mode for the ACCSystem–ACCore boundary; narrowly limited to SREQ-PH01-CONN-002. SREQ-PH01-CONN-006 is affected by the decision reference but its health-state and local-continuity semantics are shared invariants, not separate selectable paths.
multi_path_scopes.selection_context: A per-institution deployment/onboarding selector governed by security and operations policy: outbound initiation is the default for firewalled institutions; protected inbound may be selected only with explicit approval and perimeter controls. Polling, long-polling, or persistent-channel choice is an operations-controlled selection. No universal transport, inbound endpoint, authentication method, or hosting form is inferred.
multi_path_scopes.shared_contract: All paths use one logical authenticated ACCore connector contract and identical contract semantics. The boundary remains the sole integration route, binds every message to the authenticated institution, preserves ACCore ownership of ERP/product/inventory data, uses the documented Outbox/Inbox and scoped idempotency/correlation baseline, and does not permit direct ACCSystem access to the ACCore database or internal services. Concrete version/schema mapping remains subject to ADR-021/API Governance and is not invented here.

failure_recovery_audit_security: On connector interruption, the institution connectivity state is unavailable and recovery restores the state; ACCore local ERP operations continue.
Outbound work remains durable in the Outbox and is retried on reconnect; interruption is not treated as business rejection.

For uncertain reservation delivery, timeout does not prove rejection or release; preserve UNKNOWN and reconcile by reservation ID/idempotency key through an authoritative query or approved callback where supported.

Authentication is policy-selected per institution between OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials and mTLS; disabled methods are refused, credentials/certificates are rotatable and revocable, and TLS/service-to-service authentication applies.

Institution identity is bound to the authenticated principal; cross-institution access is rejected, and all traffic enters through the connector boundary. No source-supported path relaxes tenant isolation or the no-direct-database-access rule.

State/idempotency and financial authority remain fixed across paths: duplicate effects are prevented by stable keys, ACCore remains the inventory source of truth, and no payment is authorized until required reservations are authoritatively accepted. Audit/notification behavior follows the documented security and operational controls; no additional audit schema or numeric threshold is asserted.

records.rationale: The registry identifies exactly four active non-RETIRED rows carrying RP-03. The canonical sources show two valid coexisting delivery paths—synchronous response by default and institution-approved asynchronous callback—under one shared reservation contract. RP-03 should therefore be treated as a narrowly scoped mode selector for delivery, not as permission to vary state semantics, canonical vocabulary, idempotency, payment gating, authoritative expiry, release safety, or security controls. ADR-018 technically resolves the old RESERVED/INSUFFICIENT versus ACCEPTED/REJECTED ambiguity by selecting ACCEPTED/REJECTED/UNKNOWN/EXPIRED, so that portion is not a multi-path decision. The remaining delivery, query-channel, schema, policy, ownership/approval, and evidence issues must remain explicit blockers.

multi_path_scopes.source_scope: Reservation response delivery for seller-scoped reservation requests and UNKNOWN reconciliation; does not reopen the already technically resolved status vocabulary or the UNKNOWN-safe state-machine rule.
multi_path_scopes.selection_context: Selector is limited to institution-specific delivery-mode configuration at onboarding/connectivity policy: synchronous is the default; async callback may be selected only when the institution's approved policy/connectivity conditions permit it. Exact transport/schema/version mapping remains subject to API Governance and the relevant institution/security owners; no universal selection or approval is inferred.
multi_path_scopes.shared_contract: Both paths use the same logical reservation contract and ACCore authority: one stable seller-scoped idempotency key persisted before dispatch; ACCore performs the local atomic stock/reservation decision; outcomes use the canonical ACCEPTED, REJECTED, UNKNOWN, and authoritative EXPIRED vocabulary; ACCEPTED carries reservation reference, confirmed price/quantity and expiry-policy reference; definitive rejection has a reason and no hold; duplicate requests return the original result without a second hold; all required reservations must be authoritatively ACCEPTED before payment progression.

SREQ-PH02-RRC-002 / AC-PH02-RRC-002-01: a lost accepted response is resolved by query with no duplicate hold.
SREQ-PH02-RRC-002 / AC-PH02-RRC-002-02: without a query channel the system waits and escalates.
REQ-PH02-SELLER-RESERVATION / AC-PH02-RSV-006-01: progression beyond the reservation boundary requires every required reservation to be ACCEPTED.

ADR-018 acceptance tests: timeout transitions to UNKNOWN without compensation; UNKNOWN blocks payment; reconciliation to ACCEPTED does not repeat the reservation effect; contract tests use only ACCEPTED, REJECTED, UNKNOWN, or EXPIRED; elapsed TTL hint alone never marks EXPIRED.

Both delivery modes must preserve the shared contract, stable identity, at-least-once/replay-safe processing, and the same UNKNOWN/reconciliation behavior; the repository records these as planned/not executed, not as completed evidence.

failure_recovery_audit_security: If dispatch may have occurred and no response is received, record UNKNOWN rather than REJECTED; block payment and do not release, compensate, or retry with a new effect until authoritative query/reconciliation resolves the outcome.

Reconcile using reservation_id or the stable idempotency key where an agreed query/channel exists; if no agreed channel exists, wait and escalate without repeating a possible effect. A trusted callback may be one resolution path, but its availability and mapping remain a contract gate.
Only ACCore evidence can establish EXPIRED; elapsed local time or a request TTL hint is not sufficient. Release is idempotent and cannot release consumed/committed or confirmed-order-linked stock.
State invariants are REQUESTED to ACCEPTED/REJECTED/UNKNOWN, with ACCEPTED able to become RELEASE_REQUESTED, CONSUMED/COMMITTED, or authoritative EXPIRED; UNKNOWN is non-terminal and blocks payment.
Idempotency invariant: the stable key identifies the reservation effect, is retained for retry/reconciliation, and repeated requests return the original result without a duplicate hold.

Financial invariant: reservation UNKNOWN blocks payment and no financial or compensating side effect is taken until the reservation outcome is authoritatively resolved; confirmation requires all required holds and payment guards.

Security invariant: TLS is required; service-to-service authentication uses the institution policy-controlled approved method set (OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials and/or mTLS), with final enablement requiring security/institution approval.

Audit invariant: sources require auditable operational/security evidence for relevant connectivity/release-provenance mismatches and retained reconciliation evidence; no additional reservation-specific audit field or event is specified, so none is invented.

records.rationale: The registry has exactly three active RP-04-linked rows. Source text explicitly preserves two different kinds of ambiguity. For recipient handoff, CMP-INT-ORDERNOTIFY and IF-ACC-ORDER-CONFIRM explicitly allow either one projection carrying multiple roles or multiple role-specific operations, so that narrow implementation scope can share a contract and defer role mapping to a selector. For accounting, ADR-019 explicitly describes institution-local trigger timing and lists OrderConfirmed receipt versus a later configured event as source-supported modes, but its financial commitment policy is approval-required; the universal-trigger alternative and separate FinancialCommitment event cannot be treated as approved or currently selectable. Therefore multi-path treatment is narrow and does not close RP-04, CNF-006, or the parent requirement. No statuses, approvals, IDs, numeric values, or behaviors beyond the cited sources were invented.

records.rationale: The current registry has exactly nine active rows whose open_decisions field contains UNKN-001: four main requirements and five sub-requirements listed above. The canonical source defines the reference as an unresolved owner decision about per-domain SLA/availability targets, with RPO/RTO and operational thresholds explicitly unknown or policy-owned. The requirement documents preserve measurable behavior and safe uncertainty handling—such as not treating notification failure as an order-state change, not inferring delivery failure from missing updates, and exposing indicators without asserting target values—but they do not document two or more valid coexisting operational or implementation paths for the target-setting sub-scope. The connectivity alternatives, storage alternatives, and circuit-breaker mechanisms documented elsewhere address different decisions and cannot be reassigned to UNKN-001. Therefore no multi-path treatment is warranted; the reference remains an owner/policy gate pending authoritative targets, ownership, approval, and evidence.
remaining_blockers: The source defines UNKN-001 as missing SLA/availability targets for each domain; the product owner is the named owner and the discovery source says it must be revisited before C2 container design.
NFR-012 remains OPEN: each domain needs defined RPO/RTO, an assigned verification owner, scheduled backup/restore testing, and a disaster-recovery drill; no target values are present.

Operational thresholds, circuit-breaker behavior, deadlines and recovery windows remain policy configuration owned by Operations/SRE and require workload, recovery, legal and audit evidence plus approval; no numeric values may be inferred.

The affected PH-03 and PH-04 notification/indicator behaviors retain their source-defined invariants, but UNKN-001 does not select a notification channel, delivery mechanism, threshold, or recovery implementation.

Other documented gaps remain separate and must not be collapsed into UNKN-001, including PH-03 notification provider/channel uncertainty, PH-04 delivery failure/re-attempt/return semantics, and PH-04 event/API traceability gaps.

records.rationale: UNKN-002 is explicitly recorded as an unresolved compliance/data-residency/retention framework gap owned by Legal/compliance, with payment design, personal-data handling, audit retention, and POD privacy/retention depending on it. The canonical sources prescribe governance and fail-closed invariants—jurisdiction-neutral minimization, export/deletion controls, no raw card data in ACCSystem, immutable audit records, no purge before reconciliation/audit needs are satisfied, and escalation rather than unsafe auto-resolution when policy is unconfigured—but do not define two valid coexisting implementation or operational paths for the unresolved scope. ADR-017 alternatives concern how approved policy is governed, not interchangeable runtime paths for an unresolved legal decision. The no-raw-card payment behavior is already a sound mandatory constraint (NFR-006/CON-004), so it is not treated as multi-path; SREQ-PH03-PAY-007 remains in the affected registry set only because the current registry explicitly links it to UNKN-002. The broad references are therefore narrowed to the still-open compliance, residency, privacy, and retention decisions, while separate owner, provider, finance, delivery, and source-reference gates are preserved.

records.rationale: The current registry explicitly associates UNKN-005 with exactly six active requirements: payment reconciliation, allocation-level matching, settlement evidence ingestion, the ledger/settlement boundary, seller-credit separation from capture, and unresolved-settlement visibility. Canonical sources define several compatible evidence transports and a common reconciliation contract, so that narrow intake sub-scope can support a later selector. However, the sources explicitly retain direct seller credit, controlled central settlement, separate provider attempts, and externally completed/manual payments as alternatives whose selection requires provider capability, contractual permission, Finance/Legal/institution approval, and ownership/policy decisions. Therefore the broad reference is not a resolved implementation choice and must remain an owner/policy/finance/ownership gate; only evidence transport and reconciliation mechanics receive multi-path treatment. No statuses, approvals, numeric values, provider, accounting trigger, or settlement behavior were inferred.

multi_path_scopes.shared_contract: All paths must yield approved settlement evidence normalized into settlement line items and durably mapped by provider transaction/reference, payment_attempt_id, seller_order_id, and allocation_id; aggregate transactions are decomposed before comparison. The reconciliation boundary owns run and discrepancy records and alerts, reads payment records, and does not directly authorize, refund, post the ledger, declare commercial settlement finality, or mutate payment state.
source_acceptance_criteria: A provider aggregate is decomposed to allocation-level records before comparison, and each line is matched through the durable scoped mapping rather than order_id alone.
The comparison covers the source-defined gross, fee, commission, net, currency, status, and relevant operation-timestamp basis; aggregate totals are compared only after constituent mappings exist.
Unmatched, amount, status, and currency mismatches are classified as discrepancy records and alerted without changing payment state.
A supported report absence or format change visibly produces PARTIAL or FAILED as applicable and permits rerun/recovery.
Approved settlement evidence records an approved settlement status only where the provider contract and policy support it; the reconciliation component does not infer commercial settlement finality.
No credit or payout is created by capture alone, and no settlement-dependent behavior activates without approved owner values.
